rules.title: Mandatory Planning of Works under Rolling Block Programme
rules.section_page: Indian Railways (Open Lines) General Rules 1976, Rule 15.02 clause (c)
rules.original_text: Planned maintenance and asset repair or replacement or creation work shall be executed in accordance with the 'Rolling Block Programme'. Explanation.—For the purposes of this rule, 'Rolling Block Programme' means advance planning of traffic blocks or disconnections (civil, electrical, signal and telecommunication and non-interlocked work) for a duration of up to fifty-two weeks on rolling basis by adding one week plan every week after review of output of preceding week and planning for remaining weeks.
rules.normalized_summary: All planned track, signal, and electrical maintenance must be scheduled in a forward-looking 52-week rolling window updated weekly, eliminating unscheduled ad-hoc maintenance.

rules.title: Prior Sanction Required for Works Affecting Running Line Safety
rules.source_document: General Rules for Indian Railways (Open Lines) 1976
rules.original_text: No person shall commence or perform any work or operation which will alter or affect the safety or movement of trains without obtaining the prior sanction of the Station Master or traffic authority and imposing necessary traffic/power block.
rules.normalized_summary: No engineering or maintenance activity on or near running lines can start without an officially granted traffic block from the operating department.

rules.title: Exclusivity of Train Occupancy in Block Section
rules.source_document: General Rules for Indian Railways (Open Lines) 1976
rules.original_text: Block Section means that portion of the running line between two block stations on to which no running train may enter until Line Clear has been received from the block station at the other end.
rules.normalized_summary: Under the Absolute Block System, only one movement (train or track machine under block) can occupy the block section at any given time.

rules.title: Permit to Work (PTW) Mandatory for Works within 2m of 25 kV AC OHE
rules.source_document: Indian Railways AC Traction Manual (ACTM) Volume II Part I
rules.original_text: No person shall work within 2 meters of any 25 kV live OHE equipment without a valid Permit to Work (PTW) issued by an authorized traction power official after verifying isolation and earthing on both sides of the work zone.
rules.normalized_summary: Maintenance within 2m of 25 kV overhead equipment requires power shutdown, de-energization, earthing, and a signed PTW from TPC.

rules.title: Simultaneous Traffic and Power Block for Heavy Track Machines under OHE
rules.source_document: Indian Railways AC Traction Manual (ACTM) Volume II Part I
rules.original_text: When track machines (BCM, TRT, CSM tamping), rail cranes, or major civil engineering works with high vertical reach are executed under 25 kV AC OHE, a simultaneous Traffic Block and Power Block must be granted.
rules.normalized_summary: Heavy track machines with masts, jibs, or chutes operating in electrified territory require synchronized traffic and power blocks.

rules.title: Mandatory Disconnection Notice (S&T T/351) before Interlocking Intervention
rules.original_text: No signalling gear, point mechanism, track circuit, or interlocking apparatus shall be disconnected or interfered with without prior written Disconnection Notice (Form S&T T/351) served to and accepted by the Station Master on duty.
rules.normalized_summary: S&T cannot alter or disconnect points, signals, or track circuits without formal written acceptance from the Station Master.

rules.title: Standard Protection Distances for Track Obstructions on Broad Gauge
rules.source_document: General Rules for Indian Railways (Open Lines) 1976
rules.original_text: When a line is obstructed due to work, danger signals (banner flags and detonators) shall be placed at 600m and 1200m on Broad Gauge to protect the work zone from approaching trains.
rules.normalized_summary: Works requiring line obstruction must be protected by red banner flags at 600m and three detonators 10m apart at 1200m in direction of oncoming trains.

rules.title: Works Affecting Standard Moving Dimensions
rules.source_document: Indian Railways Works Manual (IRWM Jan-2026 Edition)
rules.original_text: The Senior Section Engineer (Works) / Junior Engineer (Works) shall refer to the Assistant Divisional Engineer for instructions regarding works likely to affect moving dimensions.
rules.normalized_summary: Structures, scaffolding, and staging near track must strictly adhere to the Schedule of Dimensions (SOD) to prevent fouling train envelope.

rules.title: Temporary Caution Orders over Track under Maintenance
rules.source_document: General Rules for Indian Railways (Open Lines) 1976
rules.original_text: When any portion of track is undergoing maintenance or repairs, or is not in fit condition for trains at normal speed, a caution order shall be issued and speed restriction imposed with appropriate caution indicator, speed indicator, and termination boards.
rules.normalized_summary: Post-maintenance track consolidation periods (e.g. after deep screening or manual packing) mandate specified speed restrictions (e.g. 20/30/45 km/h) before sectional speed restoration.
